palette.notes: Frames: NES-like flat colour blocks: royal-blue hero, saturated orange/red sunset skies, black voids, icy cyan and white levels. Per text: NES palette plus four extra colours to smooth shade steps.

lighting: Flat NES lighting with one or two shade steps; mood from bold background colour (sunset orange, ice blue, snowy mountain sky) rather than light on the sprite.
silhouette: Horned helmet and shovel make the hero read at a glance even very small; each boss has one signature shape (King Knight's crown and ruff, Kratos on a pillar in the crossover).

motion.timing: Not measured. Frames show few-frame NES-style sprites and long held poses during dialogue; action is short bursts between holds.

texture: Clean tiles, chunky pixel bricks and pillars, crisp black outlines; detail by colour blocks, not noise. Text boxes are black with a white border and a small portrait icon.
camera: Side-scrolling, wide shot with the play plane low in frame; parallax mountain or sky layers behind. Per text: extra horizontal room and parallax beyond NES limits, no sprite flicker.
sound: Chiptune score by Jake Kaufman for an expanded NES sound chip.

acting.enters: Boss stands on a pillar or ledge while a text box with a portrait icon plays the intro; the fight starts after the talk.
acting.acts: Strong held key poses; dialogue boxes carry the personality; a get-item box pops up mid-scene for the gag.
acting.exits: Defeated foes blink or explode and leave a short readable beat; the hero holds a victory pose.
acting.depth: Action on one plane; parallax backgrounds and big sky give depth. Characters are small in the frame.

techniques: restricted NES palette with a few extra colours
few frames, exaggerated key poses, crisp holds
black outline for readable sprites on busy backgrounds
dialogue box with a tiny portrait icon over the scene
item pop-up box as a comic beat
parallax and camera shake on an NES look
feel: flat NES palette + iconic horned silhouette + held poses with text-box banter = retro charm with modern timing
for_fred: Don't add frames to Fred; pick a few exaggerated key poses and hold them. Use an NES-style text box with a tiny Fred portrait for his lines, and give him a staged re-entrance (pose, beat, box) each time he comes back.
